newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends softer on interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends softer on interest rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine peso slipped to close at 26.374 to the dollar on Thursday following a decline in the domestic interest rate, brokers said.
The peso closed at 26.372 on Wednesday.
The Central Bank cut its overnight borrowing rate by two percentage points to 16.0 percent, creating a domino effect on the longer-termed fixed-income securities.
"Some traders just took the rate cut as an alibi to buy dollars," one trader said.
Others said the cut was expected by the market, and was too small to change investment strategy.
Trades were moderate at $136 million with done rates vacillating between 26.373 and 26.374.
The Central Bank did not intervene in the market, keeping its selling rate at 26.375.
Traders expected the exchange rate to remain stuck in the present range in the coming days.
